24.canonical: Include reasoning-intensive, multi-step tasks that require resolving indirect or scattered clues across sources to reach a specific answer.

33.canonical: Select evaluation metrics to match the reliability question: use single-run success or pass@k when one successful attempt is enough, and pass^k when every attempt must succeed consistently.

43.canonical: Populate each task's exposed tool set with the minimum necessary relevant tools plus plausible, semantically similar distractors so evaluation tests tool discovery under realistic noise without adding ambiguity.

49.canonical: Use reference trajectories for solvability checks and post-hoc diagnostics only; score pass/fail by grounded claims so valid alternative paths are not penalized.

60.canonical: Structure diagnostic judging around the verified evidence trace, expected claims, missed claims, and actual behavior so failures are localized without penalizing alternative valid plans.

61.canonical: Use one shared failure-mode vocabulary for human reviewers and automated diagnostic judges, assigning the primary root-cause mode plus contributing modes with explicit confidence and disambiguation rules.

82.canonical: Before trusting poor eval scores, verify that the tasks and graders are fair, unambiguous, and correctly configured so failures reflect agent behavior rather than broken evaluation.

85.canonical: Treat evaluations as routine development artifacts: define realistic capability evals early, iterate on them like unit tests, and use them to make progress and unstated expectations visible.

102.canonical: Treat tool-description augmentation as useful but not universal or free: apply it adaptively by domain and model while budgeting for higher execution steps and token use and watching for regressions.

110.canonical: Write tool descriptions with all core quality components present and viable: purpose, usage guidance, limitations, parameter details, and self-sufficient prose, with examples only supplementing the description.

112.canonical: Keep tool descriptions accurate and precise: state only implemented behavior, concrete constraints, parameter meanings, and boundaries, while removing ambiguous, contradictory, or self-referential wording.

116.canonical: Use source-code grounding as a reliability safeguard for tool-description faithfulness, especially for behavior- and input-tied components, while not assuming it will always improve task success.

134.canonical: Configure timeouts for long-running or streaming operations so active progress prevents premature timeout while cancellation and stream termination still resolve cleanly.

165.canonical: Provide intelligent, searchable tool discovery with adjustable detail levels once tool catalogs grow large enough that browsing or static exposure is inefficient.

168.canonical: Keep sensitive and intermediate data out of the model context by default, exposing only explicitly logged, returned, or policy-approved values through least-exposure controls such as tokenization, read-only mode, or metadata-only secret access.

169.canonical: Persist intermediate state, reusable task code, and agent memory outside the transient prompt when workflows need resume capability, repeated execution, continuity, provenance, or auditability.

171.canonical: Use deferred tool loading with a small always-loaded core and searchable long tail so full tool definitions stay out of context until needed and tool metadata remains within the context budget.

223.canonical: Bound the agent reasoning loop with an explicit maximum-iteration cap, and on retry have the evaluator return structured feedback that the planner consumes to revise the plan.

260.canonical: Use the spec diff's RFC-2119 requirement text as ground truth for SEP requirement levels and conformance cases, not the SEP summary or PR description.

261.canonical: Ship each new conformance scenario with proof it runs green against a real implementation plus a negative test that asserts the specific expected failing check.

265.canonical: Import protocol types from the vendored spec-types version that matches the scenario or connection lifecycle, and refresh those generated files rather than hand-editing them.

279.canonical: Implement SSE streams with unique stream IDs, retry and priming events, and reconnection/resumption support using Last-Event-ID, including replay after mid-operation stream closure.

286.canonical: Assess SDK tier gates from the required conformance pass rates, triage and P0 responsiveness, stable release status, documentation, dependency policy, and roadmap obligations for Tier 1 or Tier 2; otherwise classify the SDK as Tier 3.

296.canonical: Author traceability YAML by mapping each spec-diff normative sentence exactly to a check or excluded reason, leaving TODO rows for ambiguity and flagging paraphrases or unsupported keyword levels.

309.canonical: In an Inspector session, first verify connectivity and capability negotiation, then exercise each advertised capability surface through its dedicated tab with real inputs and observed results.

337.canonical: Exercise tools through the connected client session and assert both model-facing text content and machine-readable structuredContent, calling listTools first when schema validation depends on cached tool schemas.

350.canonical: Page every MCP list call with a cursor loop, collecting results until the response has no next cursor rather than assuming the first page is complete.

352.canonical: Use the SDK's built-in ping() for health checks, adding an explicit timeout or deadline when the side being called does not provide one.

353.canonical: Wire progress reporting end-to-end only when requested: the client supplies an onprogress callback/progress token and the server emits progress notifications guarded by that token.

354.canonical: Make long-running calls cancellable end-to-end: the client passes and aborts an AbortSignal, and the server handler polls the signal and stops promptly when cancellation is signalled.

358.canonical: Define and register MCP tool and prompt schemas with JSON Schema 2020-12, directly or through a compatible schema library such as Zod/Standard-Schema.

360.canonical: Use InMemoryTransport for unit, integration, test, and development in-process MCP wiring, reserving stdio, Streamable HTTP, or local server URLs for transport-level or production paths.

377.canonical: Keep agent guidance minimal, judgment-anchored, and non-overlapping across prompts, skills, CLAUDE.md, and user requests, verifying that removed constraints do not hurt behavior.
